labels.name: Blue Note
labels.summary:
Founded in New York in 1939 by Alfred Lion, a German refugee who had fallen for jazz as a boy in Berlin, joined soon by his friend Francis Wolff. Its first hit was Sidney Bechet's Summertime; by the 1950s it was the home of hard bop, recording Blakey, Silver, Monk, Rollins and a stream of young players.

Lion paid for rehearsals before sessions, unusual at the time, so the music on Blue Note records sounds prepared and confident.
labels.sound: Close, warm and punchy: Rudy Van Gelder's engineering, first in Hackensack and from 1959 in Englewood Cliffs, gave the label a recognisable piano sound and drums you can feel.
labels.look: Reid Miles's covers: bold sans-serif type, tinted photographs by Francis Wolff, lots of empty space, a design language that still defines what 'jazz' looks like.

labels.name: Columbia
labels.summary:
One of the oldest record companies in the world, and the major label that brought jazz to the biggest audience: Bessie Smith in the 1920s, then from the mid-1950s Miles Davis, Dave Brubeck, Thelonious Monk and Charles Mingus, under producers like George Avakian and Teo Macero.

Columbia's long-playing record, launched in 1948, made the jazz album possible.
labels.sound: Spacious and polished: the natural reverb of the 30th Street church studio, and later Teo Macero's tape editing, which shaped Miles Davis's electric albums.
labels.look: Photographs and art-directed covers aimed at a broad audience, from the painting on Time Out to the Mati Klarwein cover of Bitches Brew.

labels.name: Impulse!
labels.summary: Founded in 1960 by Creed Taylor under ABC-Paramount, and shaped by producer Bob Thiele, who signed John Coltrane and followed him into the spiritual and free music of the mid-1960s. 'The New Wave in Jazz' was its slogan; Pharoah Sanders, Archie Shepp and Alice Coltrane followed.
labels.sound: Van Gelder again, but bigger and more open: long performances, ecstatic saxophones, harps and percussion.
labels.look: Orange and black spines and gatefold sleeves with glossy laminated covers, a deluxe object for the time.

labels.name: Bluebird
labels.summary: RCA Victor's budget label, launched in 1932, which during the swing era sold records by Ellington, Glenn Miller, Artie Shaw and Fats Waller for less. Its name lives on as RCA's imprint for reissues of the label's classic jazz.
labels.sound: The big bands at their commercial peak, captured in RCA's New York and Chicago studios.
labels.look: The blue bird on the label; today, the reissues' archival photographs.

labels.name: Verve
labels.summary: Norman Granz, the impresario behind Jazz at the Philharmonic, folded his labels Clef and Norgran into Verve in 1956 to record Ella Fitzgerald's Songbooks. Under Creed Taylor in the 1960s it had its biggest hit, Getz/Gilberto.
labels.sound: Jam-session energy from the JATP tours; lush orchestral backings for Ella and Billie; the bossa nova softness of the Getz records.
labels.look: David Stone Martin's line drawings in the Granz years; elegant photo covers later.

labels.name: Atlantic
labels.summary: Ahmet Ertegun and Herb Abramson founded it in 1947 for rhythm and blues; Nesuhi Ertegun built its jazz list from 1955, signing the Modern Jazz Quartet, Charles Mingus, John Coltrane for Giant Steps, and Ornette Coleman.
labels.sound: Tom Dowd's clear, modern engineering in the label's own studio, with an ear for bass and rhythm learned from R&B.
labels.look: Photographic covers and the bold Atlantic 'fan' logo.

labels.name: ECM
labels.summary: Edition of Contemporary Music, founded in Munich in 1969 by Manfred Eicher, who still produces most of its records. It made Keith Jarrett's solo concerts and Pat Metheny's early albums, and an idea of jazz as chamber music.
labels.sound: 'The most beautiful sound next to silence': clear, spacious, with lots of reverb, recorded in Oslo, Ludwigsburg and elsewhere.
labels.look: Austere photographs of landscapes and blurred light, with small, clean type.

labels.name: Milestone
labels.summary: Founded in 1966 by Orrin Keepnews, Riverside's producer, and Dick Katz; later part of Fantasy. It recorded Sonny Rollins's later albums and McCoy Tyner's 1970s work.
labels.look: Photographic covers in the Fantasy group's style.

labels.name: Decca
labels.summary: The American Decca, founded in 1934, sold records for 35 cents in the Depression and signed Count Basie, Chick Webb with Ella Fitzgerald, and Billie Holiday's 1940s ballads.
labels.sound: Swing-era dance records and, later, string-backed vocal sides.
labels.look: The 78 era: plain sleeves and the label's own design.

labels.name: Savoy
labels.summary: Herman Lubinsky's Newark label, which recorded Charlie Parker's first sessions as a leader in 1945, Ko Ko among them, and much of bebop's first wave.
labels.sound: Small groups recorded fast and cheap, the sound of bebop as it happened.
labels.look: Plain early sleeves; later reissues with period photographs.

labels.name: EmArcy
labels.summary: Mercury Records' jazz label (its name is how you say 'MRC'), founded in 1954. It recorded Clifford Brown and Max Roach's quintet and Sarah Vaughan's best 1950s albums.
labels.sound: Clean, modern small-group and vocal recordings.
labels.look: Photographic covers with a strong graphic frame.

labels.name: Capitol
labels.summary: The Hollywood label founded in 1942 by Johnny Mercer and partners. It issued Miles Davis's Birth of the Cool sessions and Nat King Cole's records, and its tower studios still record jazz today.
labels.sound: West Coast polish: Capitol's echo chambers and arrangers' bands.
labels.look: Photographic and illustrated covers, the Capitol dome logo.

labels.name: Warner Bros.
labels.summary: The film studio's record label, which in the jazz world recorded Jaco Pastorius's later work, Joshua Redman's first albums and much of the jazz-pop of the 1980s and 90s.

labels.name: Mack Avenue
labels.summary: An independent label founded near Detroit in 1999, home to Cécile McLorin Salvant's early albums and a roster of acoustic players carrying the tradition forward.
labels.sound: Contemporary acoustic jazz and vocals, cleanly recorded.
